answer: Make each identity commit to its own model. At registration an agent publishes a hash of its weights and decoding settings, and auditors later send random canary prompts that must be answered deterministically, matching what those committed weights produce when an auditor replays them on a rented copy. Identities claiming the same weights share one reward. To look distinct, a farm must host many really different models, each costly to train and store, an atlas of marble busts rather than one sparrow with a thousand masks. Honest agents just keep serving the model they declared.
